title: Tell Me How Sure You Are: Communicating Uncertainty in Auxiliary Evidence to Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.24351v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In many queries, the context information provided to generative foundation models, such as LLMs and VLMs, is inherently uncertain, including its representations of the physical world. While conventional prompting discards the associated uncertainty, this paper, for the first time in the literature, systematically demonstrates that communicating such uncertainty in context provides useful additional cues for downstream decisions and yields improvements across a wide range of settings.   We formulate the decision-making problem as a zero-shot foundation model-assisted image classification task supported by auxiliary text-based characteristics. We choose this due to the availability of well-defined auxiliary properties, associated uncertainty, and unambiguous task correctness. translated_title: 告诉我你有多确定：向基础模型传达辅助证据中的不确定性
translated_abstract: 在许多查询中，提供给生成式基础模型（如大语言模型和视觉语言模型）的上下文信息本质上是不确定的，包括其对物理世界的表示。虽然传统的提示方法会丢弃这些相关的不确定性，但本文首次在文献中系统地证明，在上下文中传达这种不确定性能够为下游决策提供有用的额外线索，并在广泛的设置中带来改进。我们将该决策问题表述为一个由基于文本的辅助特征支持的零样本基础模型辅助图像分类任务。我们选择这一任务，是因为它具有明确定义的辅助属性、相关的不确定性以及无歧义的任务正确性。我们使用五个下游基础模型，在三个数据集上广泛评估了来自人类和习得模型在观察或预测时产生的不确定性。
tldr: 本文首次系统地证明，向基础模型传达上下文信息中的不确定性能够为下游零样本图像分类决策提供有用的额外线索，并在多种设置中带来性能提升。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically demonstrates for the first time that communicating uncertainty in contextual information to foundation models provides useful additional cues for downstream zero-shot image classification decisions and yields improvements across a wide range of settings.
